Enforces and implements system-wide residency policy as mandated by UCOP and the UC Regents. As one of three University staff authorized to designate residence classifications for the entire UCI campus, incumbent determines residency classifications and advises the University community regarding residency related topics. Utilizes immigration law, tax law, financial and accounting principles in assigning classifications in conformance with policy. Manages, tests, and periodically reviews electronic SLR application, including user acceptance testing and ensures application conforms to annual changes in law and policy. Accurate designation of nonresident classification has a substantial financial impact on the University with nearly 28% of incoming undergraduates paying the nonresident tuition rate, amounting to over $113M annually.

Provides protected student specific information about enrollment, grades, and other pertinent student record information. Applies professional Registrar student service based concepts to student record functions. Provides information and local enforcement of institutional, state, and federal policies, procedures, and regulations.
Successful completion of a Department of Justice (DOJ) Live Scan background check.
Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize work and meet deadlines in an environment of frequent interruptions and distractions.
Thorough knowledge of Student Information Systems, Student Billing Systems, and Online Statement of Legal Residence.
Thorough knowledge of policies, regulations, and practices with student records services.
Thorough knowledge of U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service laws, federal regulations and guidelines, and state residency statutes pertaining to residency matters.
Ability to answer several incoming phone lines in a courteous and timely manner.
Strong problem identification, critical thinking, and problem solving skills; judgment and decision-making ability. Ability to assess processes and implement improvements.
Thorough knowledge of common University-specific computer application programs and productivity software including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, email, and web browsers.
Strong written and verbal communication skills. Active listening skills. Customer service orientation. Interpersonal skills.
Thorough knowledge of University policies, processes, and procedures and of Federal and California laws pertaining to the privacy rights of students and access to student information.
Ability to apply thorough knowledge of policies to a variety of individual situations. Recommends procedures to ensure compliance in a diverse learning community.
Strong ability to establish and maintain cooperative relationships with campus departments, UC campuses, and external agencies.
Ability to work with people from diverse cultures. Utilizes excellent constituent service skills with all interactions.
